sam: Quick heads-up — did a targeted sweep comparing remat (activation checkpointing) on/off for the 8K-run on redwood-13b with PP=2 TP=4. Seeing a surprising jump in all-reduce stalls when remat is enabled on TP layers. raw profiler excerpt below. :eyes:

sam: ```
config: pp=2 tp=4 remat=on batch_tokens=32k
wall: 310s
compute: 150s (48%)
allreduce: 95s (31%)
kv-io: 20s (6%)
recompute: 45s (15%)
note: allreduce stalls overlap only 8% with recompute
```

anya: hmm — do you mean remat is increasing the time spent in allreduce (not just total)?

sam: yeah. total allreduce time up ~1.3x vs remat=off. latency tail worse. hypothesis: recompute inserts extra minibatches of activation compute that shift timing, reducing overlap window for async allreduce and causing more syncs.

jun: can you dump the timeline flame? want to see if NCCL kicks happen mid-forward or at PP boundary. Also which kernel path was used? fallback to slower matmul kernels can amplify sync costs.

sam: timeline pasted: https://internal/prof/1795122330/timeline (private) — quick excerpt: NCCL op bursts line up right after recompute segments. Kernel selection note: we fell back to fp16_avx matmul on shard 1 for some sequence lengths, others used fused_gemm_fp16.

mike: that kernel fallback probably explains part of it. Fused_gemm has better compute density so overlap with comm works; fallback reduces compute time predictability and causes more frequent short NCCL ops. Did you try gating remat only on encoder blocks vs every block?

sam: not yet. I ran remat=tp_only (remat only inside TP partitions) — improved overlap but still ~1.15x allreduce.

anya: what about batching heuristics? if recompute breaks prefix/KV cache reuse we may be getting more KV fetches which serialize before allreduce. Any change in cache hit rate?

sam: good call — KV cache hit-rate dropped from 98% -> 92% for the same request mix when remat on (weird, maybe due to timing causing stale entries to be invalidated by our cache eviction heuristic). KV-io time rose ~2x for small seqs.

jun: try two micro-experiments: (1) force fused_gemm on all devices to remove kernel variance; (2) increase async_allreduce_window in runtime config to allow more overlap with recompute.

sam: did both on a follow-up run. results: forcing fused_gemm reduced allreduce time by 22%. bumping async window from 20ms -> 80ms reduced allreduce stalls further, total wall 285s vs 310s. still ~1.08x vs remat off.

mike: sounds like multiple small effects compounding: kernel fallback, reduced KV cache effectiveness, and recompute reshuffling of the timeline that reduces natural comm/compute overlap. Nice repro.

anya: for next steps — can we add a quick patch to runtime: (a) delay KV eviction slightly when remat enabled, (b) prefer fused_gemm for those sharded sequence-length patterns, (c) add a lightweight soft-prefetch for KV before expected allreduce window. If that regresses memory, toggle behind flag.

jun: also add timeline annotation for remat segments in perf UI so we can correlate NCCL ops to recompute segments faster.

sam: logging a perf issue: PERF-4261 with attached traces + config. assigning to eng-runtime. tagging @mike @anya for kernel and caching follow-ups. :thumbsup:

sre-bot: perf-alert: regression detected on 2026-03-18 14:12 UTC for redwood-13b (pp=2,tp=4). severity: medium. linked: PERF-4261.

mike: I'll prototype fused_gemm force in a perf branch and submit a small PR for review tomorrow.

anya: I'll experiment with KV eviction tuning and run the synthetic hit-rate sweep.

jun: I'll update the profiler to overlay remat/recompute ranges. low risk.

sam: thanks folks. plan: land quick kernel patch, KV tweak behind flag, rerun full sweep. will post updated numbers in this thread. :rocket:
